## Setup
### Library
```{r}
# Library of Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(stars)
library(tmap)
library(quarto)
library(spData)
library(spDataLarge)
library(geodata)
library(terra)
library(cowplot)
```

### Set Theme
```{r}
# Set Theme
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Data Loading
```{r}
roads <- st_read('data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg.zip', query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass = 'motorway'")

buildings <- st_read('data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg.zip', query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1 WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL) OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

tx_5_07 <- rast('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif')
tx_5_16 <- rast('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif')
tx_6_07 <- rast('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif')
tx_6_16 <- rast('data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif')
```

## Data Merging
```{r}
# Combining raster tiles for each date
tx_07 <- merge(tx_5_07, tx_6_07)
tx_16 <- merge(tx_5_16, tx_6_16)
```

## Finding Locations that Experienced a Blackout

```{r}
# Checking extent, resolution, and CRS match
compareGeom(tx_07, tx_16) # true
```
```{r}
# Difference raster
tx_diff <- tx_16 - tx_07

# Reclassifying (1: >= 200, else NA)
blackout <- ifel(tx_diff <= -200, 1, NA)
```
```{r}
# Vectorising the blackout mask
blackout_vect <- as.polygons(blackout, dissolve = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Checking for invalid geometries
is.valid(blackout_vect) # true
```
```{r}
# Defining Houston rectangular polygon
houston_extent <- ext(-96.5, -94.5, 29, 30.5)

# Cropping to Houston coordinates
blackout_cropped <- crop(blackout_vect, houston_extent)
```
```{r}
# Reprojecting cropped blackout to EPSG:3083
blackout_reprojected <- project(blackout_cropped, 'EPSG:3083')

# Checking new CRS
crs(blackout_reprojected, describe = TRUE) # EPSG 3083
```

## Excluding Highways
```{r}
# Converting the roads linestrings to a SpatVector (terra)
motorways_vector <- vect(roads)

# Reprojecting the motorways to match the blackout SpatVector
motorways_reprojected <- project(motorways_vector, 'EPSG:3083')

# Creating 200 meter buffer around motorways
motorways_200_buffer <- buffer(motorways_reprojected, width = 200)

# Removing the 200 meter buffer for motorways from blackout SpatVector
blackout_no_motorways <- erase(blackout_reprojected, motorways_200_buffer)
```

## Identifying Homes that Experienced a Blackout
```{r}
# Converting building multipolygons to SpatVector (terra)
buildings_vector <- vect(buildings)

# Reprojecting the buildings to match the blackout SpatVector
buildings_reprojected <- project(buildings_vector, 'EPSG:3083')

# Clipping to buildings that experienced a blackout
buildings_blackout <- intersect(buildings_reprojected, blackout_no_motorways)
```

## Estimating Homes that Lost Power
### Estimating Total Residences
```{r}
# Finding building areas
buildings_vector$area <- expanse(buildings_vector, unit = 'm')

# Removing small, non-housing structures (<30 m^2), retaining mobile homes
residences <- buildings_vector[buildings_vector$type %in% 'static_caravan' | buildings_vector$area >= 30, ]

# Removing duplicate rows with the same ID
residences <- residences[!duplicated(residences$osm_id), ]

# Estimated total residences/homes
n_residences <- nrow(residences)
```

### Estimating Blackout Residences
```{r}
# Finding building areas
buildings_blackout$area <- expanse(buildings_blackout, unit = 'm')

# Removing small, non-housing structures (<30 m^2), retaining mobile homes
blackout_residences <- buildings_blackout[buildings_blackout$type %in% 'static_caravan' | buildings_vector$area >= 30, ]

# Removing duplicate rows with the same ID
blackout_residences <- blackout_residences[!duplicated(blackout_residences$osm_id), ]

# Estimated total blackout residences/homes
n_blackout_residences <- nrow(blackout_residences)
```

```{r}
# Estimated proportion of residences in blackout
blackout_pct = 100 * (n_blackout_residences / n_residences)
```

## Plotting and Discussion
```{r}
# Plotting where buildings has blackouts
buildings_plot <- tm_shape(buildings_blackout) + 
  tm_polygons(col = '#1B365D', fill = '#1B365D') +
tm_title('Residential Buildings', position = tm_pos_out('center', 'top'), fontface = 'bold') +
tm_scalebar(position = c('left', 'bottom'), text.size = 0.6) +
tm_compass(position = c('right', 'top'), size = 1.5) +
tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap')
```

```{r}
# Plotting where residences has blackouts
residences_plot <- tm_shape(blackout_residences) + 
  tm_polygons(col = '#1B365D', fill = '#1B365D') +
tm_title('Residences (Dwellings)', position = tm_pos_out('center', 'top'), fontface = 'bold') +
tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap')
```

### Blackouts Experienced by Residential Buildings & Dwellings
```{r}
# Arranging the blackout plots
tmap_arrange(buildings_plot, residences_plot, ncol = 2, nrow = 1)
```

_This plot displays where residential buildings and dwellings experienced blackouts in the Houston metropolitan area. The left plot shows polygons for all buildings fiting a residential profile that experienced blackout. The right plot shows the same, but for all buildings that fit a residential profile **and** have a surface area of greater than 30 square meters (~322 square feet) (to remove buildings like detached single-car garages, greenhouses, and sheds), what are essentially dwellings. They are almost identical, as the removal of small accessory structures only reduced the total residential buildings by approximately 8000 (475941 to 468091)._

```{r}
# Combining the 2/7 and 2/16 maps into one figure
tx_feb <- c(tx_07, tx_16)
names(tx_feb) <- c('February 7th', 'February 16th')

# Cropping to Houston extent
tx_feb_houston <- crop(tx_feb, houston_extent)

# Plotting
tm_shape(tx_feb_houston) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = 'inferno', trans = 'log1p'), col.free = FALSE, col.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Light Intensity (nW·cm⁻²·sr⁻¹)', position = tm_pos_out('center', 'bottom', 'center'), orientation = 'landscape', stack = 'vertical')) +
tm_facets(ncol = 2) +
tm_title('Night Light Intensity Comparison (Houston, Texas)', position = tm_pos_out('center', 'top', 'center'), fontface = 'bold') +
tm_layout(panel.label.bg.color = 'white', panel.label.color = 'black', panel.label.frame = FALSE, panel.label.fontface = 'bold') +
tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_out('center', 'bottom'), stack = 'vertical', text.size = 0.6)
```

_This plot shows the chnage in light intensity observed before and after severe storms driven by the polar vortex in February of 2021 in Houston, Texas. There is a visible loss of light intensity as many parts of the metropolitan area experienced power blackouts, which left millions without power._

**Reflection**

_Here I aimed to understand the extent and severity of the blackouts that occured because of severe storms due to the polar vortex in February of 2021 in Texas, in the metropolitan area of Houston. The night light intensity visibly decreased as a result of power outages across the region and the outages appear to be concentrated in certain areas, potentially under certain power grids. Limitations in looking at outages comes from the way that buldings appear to be classified, as I needed to clean the buildings to be of a likely residential size of greater than 30 square meters. Additonally, blackouts were modeled using remote sensing of light, as opposed to power company outage information; although light due to highways was accounted for, there could be other potential reasons for increase or decrease in light intensity outside of blackouts._
